items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I saw the gateway to East Berlin, the Russian war memorial and the stadium where Hitler had refused to shake hands with the great American Negro athlete Jessie Owens during the 1936 Olympic Games.

ctx.x: After the concert, I was invited to the most popular jazz club in Berlin, so I was told. It was the largest jazz club I had seen in Europe. It could hold about 400 people. Hans, Fritz and Tiger Jones went with me. Jones was a jazz fan as so many athletes are. There was a fine guitarist whom I met, named Rediske and I sat in with his group and the joint was really swinging. Tiger Jones could sing and not bad, so he joined the session also. He was well known there because when he was not in training, he was in this…

As this was my first time in Berlin, Hans and Fritz took me out sight-seeing the 30th. The effects of the bombings that Berlin suffered in World War II could be seen everywhere, but the bricks from the ruins were stacked in neat piles and the streets were the cleanest I've ever seen anywhere. I saw the gateway to East Berlin, the Russian war memorial and the stadium where Hitler had refused to shake hands with the great American Negro athlete Jessie Owens during the 1936 Olympic Games.

I did my second concert in a different theatre from the first one and in a different part of the city. There was a German trumpetist on the bill that night who was known as the best jazz trumpeter in Germany. His name was Macky Kasper and he was good. But his main claim to fame was that he could blow loud. He had some "iron chops" as we say in musical terms for a trumpeter. After the concert I went back to the club I had visited the night before and jammed with the cats again. Tiger Jones was also on the scene.…
